title: Diffusion Language Model Parallel Decoding via Product-of-Experts Bridge
claim: Direct one-shot correction of a weak proposal yields short accepted chunks; splitting it through an intermediate distribution gives longer chunks and better quality.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, top-to-bottom steps, shared prompt banner and legend, outcome banners at bottom
description: A full-width banner at the top gives the prompt "Solve: 12 + 7 =", and a color-coded legend sits below it. Legend entries are DLM draft token, accepted by RS, rejected → correction, discarded suffix, appended chunk, and selected candidate / IS weight. Panel (A), "Direct DLM → AR correction", shows naive speculative sampling in three steps. Each step has a row of draft tokens, a row of green accepted and orange rejected tokens, and a row of blue appended tokens. Only short prefixes get accepted. It ends with an orange outcome box reading "short accepted chunks → high latency". Panel (B), "PoE-Bridge two-step correction", shows a single step. Three parallel drafts (k=1, 2, 3) go through rejection sampling toward the PoE distribution. The k=2 row is highlighted with a blue border and a star, and it is fully accepted. Importance weights w1, w2 and w3 follow, then the appended chunk. A green outcome box at the bottom reads "longer accepted chunks + closer-to-AR IS candidates → high quality + low latency". The eye goes first to the colored token rows and the highlighted k=2 row.
caption: Comparison between naive speculative sampling and PoE-Bridge. (A) Naive speculative sampling directly corrects DLM drafts from pD to the AR target pAR. Due to the large proposal–target mismatch, direct verification often accepts only short prefixes, resulting in limited throughput gains. (B) PoE-Bridge splits this difficult correction into two easier stages: speculative rejection sampling first moves DLM drafts toward the intermediate bridge distribution pPoE, and importance sampling then refines the accepted candidates toward pAR. Because pPoE is closer to both the DLM proposal and the AR target, PoE-Bridge achieves longer accepted chunks and more stable importance weights, enabling high generation quality and low latency.
abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer substantial speed advantages through parallel decoding, but the lack of token dependencies limits generation quality compared to autoregressive (AR) models. Recent progress attempts to bridge the gap via importance sampling, with DLM being the proposal and AR being the target. However, due to the huge gap between their distributions, the sampling requires a large number of particles and is thus expensive to compute. In this paper, we introduce PoE-Bridge, a novel decoding framework that drastically improves generation speed and accuracy by introducing an intermediate distribution to bridge the gap. The distribution is constructed as a Product-of-Experts (PoE) of the DLM proposal and the AR target. With the intermediate distribution, we first use the DLM to draft multiple continuations in parallel, then apply rejection sampling to verify the drafted tokens and move the resulting candidates toward the PoE. We then use importance sampling to further correct the PoE-aligned candidates toward the AR target. We further propose several improved techniques, including mixed-temperature sampling for enhanced diversity and elastic rejection windows for reducing wasted verification. Empirically, PoE-Bridge achieves significantly improved accuracy with $5\times$ speedup over the standard DLM decoding approach, and recovers at least 95% of the target AR model's performance, efficiently advancing most of the quality gap on challenging mathematical reasoning and coding tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/juntongshi48/poe-bridge.
